why: Both analyses land on the same convenience / profit-per-visit hedgehog and the key brutal facts, but Analysis 1 correctly recognises the subject as already great and limits its stop-doing list to the real temptations (scale acquisitions, a standalone PBM, re-diversification, marginal sites). Analysis 2 is sharp and adds useful derived arithmetic, but it rates the company merely "good" and prescribes more intervention (deferring new metros, eight stop-doing items), which shows less restraint toward a proven core.
